title: IMPACTNet: Unifying Auto-bidding in End-to-End Merged Auctions

problem.claim: Merged-auction mechanisms must coordinate advertiser conversion value, platform revenue and reputation, user experience, advertiser tROS constraints, and duplicate ad-organic items in an autobidding setting.

gap.claim: Existing studies often overlook autobidding in merged auctions and fail to address the resulting multi-stakeholder challenge.

contributions.claim: IMPACTNet is an end-to-end framework based on automated mechanism design that learns a unified allocation and pricing mechanism.
The framework incorporates advertiser tROS constraints, uses a transformer-based architecture for contextual information, and applies a learnable state-aware de-duplication strategy.
The mechanism is formulated as constrained optimization to ensure Auto-bidding Incentive Compatibility, making truthful tROS reporting a dominant strategy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and large-scale industrial datasets reportedly show that IMPACTNet significantly outperforms established baselines.
The authors report a better balance among platform objectives, user experience, and advertiser tROS satisfaction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Merged mechanisms place sponsored ads alongside organic results according to platform rules.
Autobidding, duplicate ad-organic items, and competing stakeholder objectives make the setting complex, while existing work leaves important aspects unaddressed.
IMPACTNet learns a unified allocation and pricing mechanism with tROS constraints, contextual modeling, and state-aware de-duplication.
Constrained optimization is used to ensure truthful tROS reporting is a dominant strategy.
The authors report improved baseline performance and balance across platform, user, and advertiser objectives on synthetic and industrial datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework jointly models constraints, contextual information, and de-duplication within a unified mechanism.

interpretation.claim: In complex allocation systems, integrating interacting constraints and context into one learned mechanism may address failures caused by optimizing isolated components.

application.claim: Use an end-to-end constrained design when allocation, pricing, incentives, and duplicate-item handling are interdependent.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this integration transfers beyond merged online advertising auctions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or proof details for the AIC guarantee.
